messages:
Maya (oncall-sre): :rotating_light: seeing interconnect flaps into eu-south1 since 13:02 UTC. GPU allocation requests timing out (~502) and queue depth spiking. Auto-failover routing to eu-west2 has started but we're seeing a cross-region egress surge and higher latencies for affected customers.

Liam (infra-eng): Confirmed — fabric telemetry shows intermittent packet loss on the south1 interconnect. 8 of 12 hosts reporting elevated RX errors, and kube-scheduler is backing off pods into pending. I've opened a ticket with the provider (INC-4521).

Maya (oncall-sre): Thanks. Immediate ask: (1) draft a short status page update, (2) notify support to prep customer DMs for the most affected accounts, (3) enable stricter burst-throttling for public-tier to preserve capacity for reserved fleets.

Oliver (eng-ml): For customers on larger models we can temporarily route requests to smaller quantized variants (m-quant-1 / m-quant-2) with a fallback header. Should reduce GPU footprint by ~30-45% in the deg zones. I'll prepare a runtime flag.

Liam (infra-eng): Doing throttling now: set public-tier max_burst to 40% of baseline and reduce concurrency cap on new pods. Also toggling cross-region routing policy from "latency-first" -> "cost-conscious-fallback" to prefer local degraded nodes before egress.

Eva (support): I'll draft customer-facing copy. Quick question: do we call out potential additional egress costs if we route to other regions? Some customers want to know.

Maya (oncall-sre): Short answer: yes, some customers will see a small spike in egress billing if we shift heavy traffic cross-region. For the status page, keep it concise and safety-first. Draft below — please review/edit then I can publish.

Maya (oncall-sre): ```Status page (draft):
Incident: Capacity degradation in eu-south1
Impact: Some customers may see increased latency, 5xx errors, or degraded throughput. We have initiated automatic failover to nearby regions.
Current status: Mitigation in progress — traffic is being shifted and transient throttles are in effect to preserve capacity for reserved workloads.
ETA: 45-90 minutes for stabilization; updates every 15 minutes.
Notes: We may route some workloads cross-region temporarily; this can cause increased egress usage.
```

Grace (status-bot): Suggested next steps: (a) publish the above draft to status page as "investigating" then update to "mitigating" after 2nd update; (b) pin the support DM template to #support; (c) schedule post-incident cost review.

Eva (support): Customer DM template (concise): "Hi — we're investigating a capacity issue in eu-south1 that may affect latency or cause 5xxs. We're shifting traffic and applying mitigations. ETA 45-90m. If you're on reserved capacity, your traffic has priority; if you see billing spikes please contact us and we'll review. — Redwood Support". Thoughts?

Oliver (eng-ml): LGTM. Also adding an opt-in header for customers who want zero-eject routing (if they can accept degraded latency instead of cross-region billing). I'll open a PR for the runtime flag.

Liam (infra-eng): Provider status update: they acknowledged packet loss and are working on an isolated fabric hardware replacement. Provider ETA ~2hrs, but our mitigations should stabilize most customers sooner.

Maya (oncall-sre): Ok final plan: publish status draft as investigating now, support to send targeted DMs for high-impact customers (Eva), throttle public-tier and enable quantized fallbacks (Liam + Oliver). Finance, please note potential short-term egress spend — I'll flag for review.

Eva (support): Sent DM to top-10 affected customers and started a private thread for any escalations. Marking as "support on standby". :thumbsup:

Maya (oncall-sre): Publishing status page now. I'll update this thread in 15 mins with latest telemetry. If anyone sees critical regressions, ping here and @Maya (oncall-sre).

Grace (status-bot): Status page: incident posted -> investigating. Next automated update scheduled in 15 minutes.

Liam (infra-eng): Quick note on logs: collecting pcap snippets and increased debug sampling. Dropping artifacts into s3://redwood-incident/2160005432/ for postmortem.

Maya (oncall-sre): Thanks all. Handoff to day SRE in 30m unless we escalate. :white_check_mark:
